exposure: Patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) with dexmedetomidine (DEX) and sufentanil (SUF)
Patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) with dexmedetomidine (DEX) and nalbuphine (NAL)
patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) of dexmedetomidine (DEX) with nalbuphine (NAL)
outcome: Adverse reactions (postpartum respiratory depression, nausea/vomiting, urinary retention, cardiovascular events)
cohort: 300 women who underwent cesarean section surgery with combined spinal-epidural anesthesia
finding: Adding nalbuphine (NAL) to patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) with dexmedetomidine (DEX) was more effective in reducing visceral pain after cesarean section compared to sufentanil (SUF) with DEX, with fewer adverse reactions and higher patient satisfaction.
mod_finding: This study examined pain management strategies after cesarean delivery but did not compare different modes of delivery.
